items.title: Self Assessment 31 January Checklist (UK)
items.description: Everything to gather before the 31 January 2027 Self Assessment deadline: UTR, login, income, expenses and mileage.

items.title: HMRC Mileage Rate 2026/27: 55p a Mile
items.description: The simplified expenses mileage rate for cars and vans is 55p a mile for the first 10,000 miles in 2026/27, then 25p.

items.title: The £1,000 Trading Allowance Explained
items.description: Side hustle income under £1,000 a year may be covered by the trading allowance. Above that, you'll usually need to register.

items.title: Allowable Expenses Sole Traders Forget (UK)
items.description: Business share of your phone, use-of-home flat rate, bank fees, software and mileage. Don't miss allowable expenses.

items.title: Self Assessment Deadline: 31 January 2027
items.description: The online filing and payment deadline for the 2025/26 tax year is 31 January 2027.

items.title: Late Self Assessment Penalty: £100 and Rising
items.description: Missing the Self Assessment deadline means an automatic £100 penalty, even if you owe no tax, with more after 3 months.

items.title: Working From Home Flat Rate for Sole Traders
items.description: HMRC simplified expenses for working from home: £10, £18 or £26 a month depending on hours.

items.title: How Much to Set Aside for Tax When Self-Employed
items.description: Put a percentage of your profit aside every time you're paid so the Self Assessment bill isn't a shock.

items.title: What to Include on a UK Invoice
items.description: A unique number, your details, the customer's details, date, what you supplied and the total. Simple UK invoice checklist.

items.title: How to Chase a Late Invoice
items.description: A simple schedule to chase late payment: polite reminder on the due date, firmer at 7 days, final notice at 14.

items.title: What to Record in a Business Mileage Log
items.description: Date, start and end, purpose and miles for every business journey. Keep it in a mileage log.

items.title: Is Client Entertainment Tax Deductible? (UK)
items.description: Business entertainment like client lunches isn't an allowable expense for sole traders.

items.title: Self Assessment Payments on Account Explained
items.description: Payments on account are two advance payments towards next year's tax, due 31 January and 31 July.

items.title: VAT Registration Threshold: £90,000
items.description: You must register for VAT if your taxable turnover goes over £90,000 in a rolling 12 months.

items.title: First Steps as a New Sole Trader (UK)
items.description: Register with HMRC, open a separate account, keep receipts, track income and expenses and set aside tax.

items.title: How Long to Keep Self-Employed Records (UK)
items.description: Sole traders should keep business records for at least 5 years after the 31 January submission deadline.

items.title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: Thresholds
items.description: MTD for Income Tax starts April 2026 for qualifying income over £50,000 and April 2027 for over £30,000.

items.title: Claiming Mixed-Use Expenses as a Sole Trader
items.description: If something is used partly for business, claim the business share only, such as 50% of your phone bill.

items.title: 5 Ways to Get Invoices Paid Faster
items.description: Invoice straight away, show a clear due date and bank details, use a payment reference and send reminders.

items.title: Simplified Mileage vs Actual Car Costs
items.description: If you claim simplified mileage for a vehicle, you can't also claim fuel, insurance or repairs for it.

items.title: Etsy Seller Tax Basics for UK Sellers
items.description: Etsy payouts count as income and Etsy fees as expenses. Keep monthly records for Self Assessment.

items.title: 2 Minutes a Week Beats a January Panic
items.description: Log income and expenses weekly and your Self Assessment return takes minutes, not a weekend.

items.title: HMRC Expense Categories for Self-Employed
items.description: The main HMRC expense categories on the self-employment pages, from travel to accountancy fees.

items.title: Why Freelancers Need a Separate Bank Account
items.description: A separate account for business income and costs makes record-keeping and Self Assessment easier.

items.title: Do Your Self Assessment in One Evening
items.description: With records ready, filing your Self Assessment can take one evening: totals, file online, pay.

items.title: Check Your HMRC Login Before January
items.description: Sign in to your HMRC online account early. Fixing access can take time before the deadline.

items.title: Invoice Numbering for Sole Traders
items.description: Use unique, sequential invoice numbers and ask clients to use them as the payment reference.

items.description: The self-employed income, expenses and mileage tracker plus invoice template in one UK bundle.

items.title: Can't Pay Your Self Assessment Bill?
items.description: File on time and contact HMRC about a payment plan. Free help is available from tax charities.
